examples.text: Die Formulierung eines guten Bewerbungsschreibens bereitet vielen Leuten Schwierigkeiten.
„Wie viel von all diesen Formulierungen ihm selber einfielen und wie viel ihm die Kommunisten ins Papier schrieben, ist heute nicht mehr auszumachen.“
„Wenn du als Besucher deinen Blick über die Wände der ägyptischen Tempel wandern lässt, wirst du sehr bald auf zahlreiche Beispiele dieser Formulierung stoßen.“
„Solche sehr suggestiv vorgebrachten, sich wiederholenden Formulierungen ließen sogar einige nationalistische Kritiker den Roman über das Leben in den Schützengräben preisen.“
„Damit die Formulierung nicht so großformatig daherkommt, sei sie erläutert.“

glosses: eine spezielle Zusammenstellung von chemischen oder pharmazeutischen Komponenten, um ein Medikament mit einer genau definierten pharmazeutischen Wirkung zu erstellen

examples.text: Auf Grund seiner speziellen Formulierung tritt die Wirkung des neuen Medikaments bereits wenige Minuten nach seiner Einnahme ein.

glosses: Any mathematical rule expressed symbolically.

examples.text: x=(-b±√)/(2a) is a formula for finding the roots of the quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0.

glosses: A symbolic expression of the structure of a compound.

examples.text: H₂O is the formula for water.

glosses: A plan or method for dealing with a problem or for achieving a result.

examples.text: The company's winning formula includes excellent service and quality products.

Shakespeare has gone back to the formula of last season, by encouraging his players to press high up the pitch and restoring Shinji Okazaki to the starting XI to scurry around between midfield and attack.
Delays, large and small, have a huge variety of causes, so there is no magic formula for preventing them.

glosses: A formulation; a prescription; a mixture or solution made in a prescribed manner; the identity and quantities of ingredients of such a mixture.

examples.text: The formula of the rocket fuel has not been revealed.

glosses: A fixed phrase or set of words intended to be interpeted non-literally, typically used attitudinally or as part of convention; a formulation.

examples.text: Avoid the typical epistolic formalae, such as "Kind regards".

glosses: A formal statement of doctrine.

examples.text: The extract from the Missal of Constance, which was printed before the editio princeps […] does not contain the formulae for Advent, Sundays after Epiphany, Lent and the Sundays after Easter and Pentecost; […]

glosses: Ellipsis of infant formula, drink given to babies to substitute for mother's milk.

examples.text: They tried switching formulas, and it seemed to work: the baby seemed more content while feeding.
Many women advocate for formula, insisting that women who advocate breast-feeding have become self-righteous “lactavists,” as one writer puts it.

glosses: A syntactic expression of a proposition, built up from quantifiers, logical connectives, variables, relation and operation symbols, and, depending on the type of logic, possibly other operators such as modal, temporal, deontic or epistemic ones.
A declaration or remark.

examples.text: make a statement
publish a statement
utter a statement

glosses: A presentation of opinion or position.
A document that summarizes financial activity.

examples.text: a bank statement

glosses: An instruction in a computer program, especially one that returns no value, as opposed to a function call.

examples.text: In this section we will examine BASIC's primary statement for repeating a string of statements under program control: the FOR statement. Another statement, the NEXT statement, is always used with a FOR statement.
However, it is the responsibility of the programmer to ensure that the control ultimately reaches the last statement of the range.

glosses: Decisive.

examples.text: Gabriel Martinelli scored a dramatic late winner as Arsenal earned a statement victory over defending Premier League champions Manchester City at Emirates Stadium.

glosses: To provide an official document of a proposition, especially in the UK, a Statement of Special Educational Needs.
A choice of words and the style in which they are used in a given context.

examples.text: It is highly improbable that the drafter of the notice ever visualised the form that heavy vehicles of the future would take, but the comprehensive wording still covers modern types.
